g.text: Only four series in the dataset are measured often enough to fit a trend

text.style: font-size: 10.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: What it shows: the growth rate behind each series Epoch's regression control can fit, as an annual multiple and the

text.style: font-size: 10.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: doubling time it implies. Only 4 of the tracked series reach the 12 observations a log-linear fit requires; every other

text.style: font-size: 10.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: company is measured too sparsely to carry a trend at all.

g.text: Note: Fitted by ordinary least squares through log10 of the metric against date, over the observed points only and never extended past the

g.text: last of them. A doubling time is the fit restated, not a separate measurement. Anthropic's revenue fit is the steepest series in the

g.text: entire dataset. Companies below the threshold are counted, not fitted - a two-point 'trend' is a line through two points, not a
